decision_conditions:
Reason : 1 - The developer has provided insufficient information to enable the authority to establish whether the proposed development complies with the conditions, limitations or restrictions specified in Class J applicable to the development in question. The Local Planning Authority is unable to assess the design or external appearance of the development, and the impact of glare on occupiers of neighbouring land in the absence of proposed elevations and glint and glare details.
The proposal is therefore contrary to Condition J.4 of Schedule 2 Part 14 Class J of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (as amended).
description: The proposed installation covers Unit B1, Parkway TE, Heston as shown within the site location and proposed PV roof layout plans. The proposed installation has been designed to minimise the visual impact to the surrounding area. The panels are on pitched roof areas and they are unlikely to be seen from ground level. All equipment other than the panels themselves will be installed out of sight. The roof areas will be utilised for the installation of panels with the following proposed system: 122kWp panels (approximately 268 panels) East and West facing system across the whole site, all of which will be mounted between 6 and a 10 degree pitch, and will not protrude more than 200mm from the roof plane. The panels will not come within 1.5 meters of the roofs edge. Drawings attached. The proposed use of installation is to generate renewable electricity for use within the building. The installation proposed will feed into one of the main supplies. The technology being installed aims to reduce carbon emissions and the impact of the building on the environment. The solar panels to be used in this project are dark blue/black, do not reflect light and have anti glare covering. In addition, the panels are static and have no moving parts, neither internally nor externally. The solar PV array will not generate noise. The proposed installation will be installed by a government certified (MCS) solar PV engineering contractor, who has undertaken numerous similar projects. The proposed installation will not alter or restrict the use of the building in any way whatsoever.
